The Little Yellow Caboose

by Kent Griswold
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:39
Instaread

Every month, I’m reminded that tiny living isn’t really about the house. It’s about what comes after you make the decision to live with less.

Learning A New Language Online

Discover more
Accessing Creative Writers Resources
Blog
Decorating Home Living Spaces

We take a look behind-the-scenes at Wind River  Homes and see what goes into building some beautiful tiny  homes, modular homes, and cabins. It’s funt to learn how these homes come together in preparation for the buyer.

Joshua Becker shares something many of us need to hear. Life feels busy, rushed, and packed from morning until night. The answer isn’t about finding more time. It’s doing less of what doesn’t matter so we have time for what does.

We’ve also been following Laura LaVoie’s tiny house journey for years. Like many of us, her story has taken a new direction. She’s no longer living tiny, and it’s a reminder that life changes. Tiny living isn’t always the final destination. Sometimes it’s just one chapter of your story.

And if you’re planning to stay in your  home for years to come, don’t miss our article on aging in place. A few simple changes today can make a big difference tomorrow.

No matter where you are on your own journey I hope you find something in these pages that encourages you to keep moving forward.
